summary: Initialized active v2 Bootstrap Planning Ledger for exact placeholder feature token `<feature name>`, registered it in ledger_registry.json, captured the collaborator planning persona and ledger-only constraints, and opened q-0001 to ask what we are working on before accepting product requirements.

Jared clarified the ledger covers `a bunch of miscellaneous things`; the first item is seeing historical documents made by PM wizards, meaning Plans and PRD docs created by the wizard, plus historical Orchestrator runs. GUI design is required and likely belongs on the Orchestrator page.

Jared accepted default final/approved document output visibility with user expansion to show everything, accepted all proposed historical run actions, and confirmed the existing Orchestrator History tab as the GUI home.

Jared accepted current-project lock for Orchestrator History, accepted final/approved output retention forever by default with retention/archive handling for expanded draft/intermediate history, and accepted document-specific row actions.
Jared accepted dense default History rows, accepted the Approved only vs All history per-project control, and required deep document comparison in MVP rather than deferring deeper comparison.

Jared answered `all of thodse`, accepting all proposed History export granularities for MVP: selected-row export, multi-select bundle export, and whole filtered-view export with an identity-preserving manifest.
Jared accepted all proposed export formats/profiles, accepted a combined deep comparison UI, and specified that archived records appear only after an extra Include archived control.

Jared said `yes`, accepting the recommended project-scoped unified History index/projection as the source-of-truth shape for the History surface instead of direct ad hoc subsystem queries at view time.

Jared said `yes`, accepting rebuildable unified History projection lifecycle semantics: rebuild from immutable source records, update from wizard/run/artifact/evidence/archive/lineage/manifest events, and detect/surface stale or out-of-sync state.

Jared said `sounds good`, accepting degraded-mode behavior for stale/out-of-sync History projections: read-only viewing with visible warning, a Rebuild action, and compare/export/reopen/send-forward blocked until rebuild succeeds.

Jared said `yes`, requesting a pre-compile pressure-test pass. The pass found five remaining underspecified surfaces for the first History item and proposed MVP defaults for row schema, permissions/redaction export profiles, search/filter syntax, empty states, and acceptance tests.

Jared said `yes`, accepting the pressure-test MVP defaults bundle for exact row schema fields, permissions/redaction export profiles, structured filter-chip search, explicit empty/degraded states, and acceptance-test coverage.
Jared said `next item`, choosing to continue the miscellaneous-feature ledger to the next item rather than pause or compile the accepted History item to canonical Plans.

Jared described the next miscellaneous item: `Could we adopt something like this` `https://github.com/alfaoz/opencode-see-image` for `models models without vision`, asked to pull the repo and see how it works, and noted PM would need to adapt it because `that is for Opencode`. The repo was inspected in `/tmp/pm-ext-opencode-see-image` at commit `cde1615f6dfc9039c58da6813112ee53391b5b49`.

Jared answered the four open vision-bridge questions: `1. yes`, `2. yes`, `3. not deferred`, and `4. Yes, but the pop up has something like reject, accept, always accept(doesnt have to be that exact wording) and when you do always, it stops asking.`

Jared said `ok do that`, requesting the pressure-test pass for the accepted PM-native vision bridge item. The pass found eight implementation-readiness defaults to confirm: failure/degraded handling, image source precedence, always-accept scope/revocation, cache invalidation, redaction/sensitivity handling, bridge prompt/output schema, provider retry/cost behavior, and acceptance-test coverage.

Jared said `yes`, accepting the vision bridge pressure-test defaults bundle: fail-closed degraded states, deterministic image-source precedence, scoped/revocable always-accept permission, cache invalidation keys, redaction/disclosure policy, structured bridge prompt/output contract, explicit provider retry/cost/reroute behavior, and MVP acceptance-test coverage.

Jared corrected the item framing to the `Teach` feature with the `Teacher` persona, then asked to try again. Live Plans review found existing Teach durable-capture behavior and an existing protected `teacher` Persona, but gaps remain for Teach-specific low-end model defaults/settings, PM knowledge substrate, Teacher-guided GUI control, help-icon launch into a new Assistant Chat thread, summon phrases, activity transparency, and acceptance tests.

Jared said `sure`, accepting the Teach implementation-readiness defaults bundle, then asked whether Teach had already been specced out and implementation-ready. The finding is: existing Plans were partially specced, with Teach durable memory capture and the protected Teacher persona already present, but the integrated Teach/Teacher user-facing guided-help feature was not implementation-ready until the missing defaults were captured in this ledger.

Jared asked whether the newly added or formerly underspecced Teach items are fully specced now. The ledger answer is yes at the product-intent / future ledger-to-Plans compile level: the known Teach/Teacher gaps are now accepted with no open product questions, while canonical Plans and implementation/build decomposition still require explicit later phases.

Jared challenged whether Teach had enough detail for how it works, how it looks, where it gets information from, and how it shows the user. The ledger status was refined: behavior/source-of-truth intent is covered, but concrete GUI presentation details are not yet fully specified. A candidate GUI-detail bundle was added under q-0026.

Jared asked whether Help/Glossary is specced out and said to spec out the rest. Live Plans review found Help/Glossary has a general architecture: three-depth help, canonical help entries, related-concept clusters, and a help-entry template. The missing Teach-specific layer is now captured as candidate defaults under q-0027, superseding the narrower GUI-only q-0026.

Jared accepted q-0027 but corrected that recording the Teach Help/Glossary gap is not the same as filling it: `I accept it but i dont think we finished speccing it out right? You just recorded the gap. We need to fill it right?` The ledger marks q-0027 answered, accepts its coverage defaults, records the correction, and opens q-0028 with a concrete Teach Help/Glossary content pack.

Jared said the collaboration style is not working: `You are not collaborating with me. you need to change your style of interacting. This isnt working. I ahve no idea what you are doing or if you are doing what needs to be done. Are you filling in all the gaps?` The ledger must preserve this as a process correction: future Teach planning responses should show the gap map, status, proposed fills, and remaining decisions in user-visible form before claiming readiness.

Jared said `ok lets work through all those`. The ledger expanded beyond q-0028 Help/Glossary content into a full Teach gap-fill bundle covering readiness matrix, model setting states, PM knowledge substrate, source confidence states, help icon launch, summon phrase disambiguation, Teacher thread presentation, guided GUI action taxonomy, overlay presentation, degraded states, activity transparency, memory capture UI, handoff boundaries, end-to-end tests, and PM knowledge pressure tests. These are candidate defaults under q-0029, not accepted product intent yet.

Jared said `I accept the bundles`, accepting q-0029. Jared then directed that for the GUI we need to look at `PMConcept.html`, preserving that it `isnt the final form`, is `just a concept`, but will help `figure the gui out for these features`. Jared also clarified: `The assistant chat window and threads are modeled in the concept too.` The ledger accepted the full Teach gap-fill bundle and added PMConcept GUI concept-reference atoms for Teach/Assistant Chat threads, History, and vision bridge alignment.

Jared asked whether all items discussed so far are truly fully specced out and implementation ready. The recheck found: History, PM-native vision bridge, and Teach/Teacher have accepted ledger-level product/spec intent with no open questions or candidate atoms, and the ledger validator passes. However, strict code-implementation readiness is not yet achieved because no explicit compile has produced canonical Plans/PlanUnits, owner-doc placement, PlanUnit index/readiness evidence, or implementation task packets. Record the distinction so future responses say ledger-ready/future-compile-ready, not strict implementation-ready.

Jared asked again whether all discussed items are fully specced out and implementation ready. The answer is deliberately split: History, PM-native vision bridge, and Teach/Teacher are accepted and product-spec complete at the conversational ledger level with no open product questions/candidate atoms; read-only owner checks found no accepted History or vision product atom requiring deferral.
